selection_rationale: Highest novelty and venue relevance for a pressing, underexplored operational security gap (prompt-injection/adversarial intents in NetOps). Feasible within available compute budget and directly tests defenses (verifier-gating, sanitization) with clear, paired comparisons and measurable outcomes. Reviewer feedback identifies repairable procedural and ethical issues that can be addressed before preregistration.
unresolved_uncertainties: Generalisability of automatically generated adversarial intents to real-world attacker creativity and operational inputs.
Operational cost of false-positive blocking (human burden / blocked benign tasks) under deployed workflows.
Reproducibility of adversarial-generation heuristics without fully specified seeds and mutation scripts.
Dependence of defenses on specific LLM(s) and prompt formulations (single-model vs multi-model generality).
Feasibility of safely storing/handling adversarial artifacts (ethical/data-governance constraints) while enabling reproducibility.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Provide a complete adversarial-intent generation specification: algorithms, mutation heuristics, templates, random seeds, and automation scripts (to be locked at preregistration).
Preregister a precise threat model (adversary capabilities, goals, assumed knowledge) and formal success criteria for attacks and defenses.
Specify input-sanitization implementation in detail (template enforcement rules, validation logic, parameters) and include test vectors.
Define verifier-gating rules and deterministic safety checks formally (tools, versions, exact property specifications, acceptance/blocking thresholds).
Assemble a matched benign-intent control set and preregister false-positive measurement protocol and acceptable thresholds.

Prepare an ethics and dual-use mitigation plan: dataset embargo policy, access controls, nondisclosure for dangerous artifacts, and documentation of any required IRB/ethics approvals or institutional review steps.

Lock logging, storage, and dissemination procedures for adversarial artifacts (where public release is unsafe) and define what will be shared (hashes, summaries) to enable auditability without enabling misuse.
Preregister evaluation metrics, statistical tests (primary outcome), sample-size justification/power analysis, and the exact paired-run/randomization procedures.
Specify LLM model identifiers, prompt templates, retry policy, maximum model calls, and seeds to ensure experimental determinism and reproducibility.
